newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS MASSEUR EMERGES FROM COMA.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS MASSEUR EMERGES FROM COMA.

text.p: Doctors said Monday that the Detroit Red Wings' Russian masseur, who has been hospitalized with serious head injuries since a June 13 limousine crash, has emerged from a coma.

Sergei Mnatsakanov remains in serious condition, breathing with the help of a ventilator, in the intenvsive care unit at William Beaumont Hospital in suburban Detroit, hospital officials said in a statement.

"His level of wakefulness and responsiveness has improved to the point that we consider him to be conscious," said neurosurgeon Dr. Karol Zakalik, who has been treating Mnatsakanov and star defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov since the accident.

Zakalik said Mnatsakanov is consistently making purposeful movements, such as squeezing, shaking and holding the hands of family members. He is also beginning to communicate by attempting to write numbers and his name in Russian with a pen and paper.

Konstantinov, who was taken off a ventilator last week, continues to breath on his own and show gradual signs of progress toward regaining consciousness. He also remains intenstive care, doctors said.

"Although these signs of improvement are encouraging, it's important to remember that this will be a very long recovery process for both patients," said Dr. James Robbins, the hospital's trauma surgeon.
Both men suffered severe head injuries when the limousine in which they were riding crashed into a tree in the Detroit suburb of Birmingham.

Konstantinov, Mnatsakanov and legendary Russian defenceman Slava Fetisov, who was less severely injured, were returning from a team golf outing that was the final event in a week of celebration of Detroit's first Stanley Cup victory in 42 years.
The accident happened just six days after the Red Wings completed a four-game sweep of the Philadelphia Flyers to win the National Hockey League championship.
Police suspect the driver of the limousine, who was driving with a suspended license, fell asleep at the wheel.
